p: entered into a ship: Sins are the cause of our afflictions, and Christ only forgives them if we believe.
own city: Into Capernaum, for as Theophylact says, Bethlehem brought him forth, Nazareth brought him up, and Capernaum was his dwelling place.
seeing their faith said unto the: Knowing by a manifest sign.
blasphemeth: To blaspheme, signifies among the divines, to speak wickedly: and among the more eloquent Greeks, to slander.
And as Jesus passed forth from: Christ calls the humble sinners unto him, but he condemns the proud hypocrites.
receipt of custom: At the table where the tax was received.

sinners came and sat down with: The publicans who were placed by the Romans, after that time Judea was brought into the form of a province, to gather the taxes, and therefore by the rest of the Jews they were called sinners, that is to say, very vile men.
Then came to him the disciples: That is, wicked rivalry in matters of small importance.
children of the bridechamber mourn: A Hebrew idiom, for they that are admitted into the marriage chamber are as the bridegroom's closest friends.
new cloth unto an old garment: Raw, which was never processed by the fuller.
While he spake these things unto: There is no evil so old, and incurable, which Christ cannot heal by and by, if he is touched with true faith, but lightly as it were with the hand.
And when Jesus came into the: Even death itself gives place to the power of Christ.
minstrels and the people making a: It appears that they used minstrels at their mournings.
And when Jesus departed thence: By healing these two blind men Christ shows that he is the light of the world.
As they went out: An example of that power that Christ has over the devil.
But when he saw the multitudes: Although the ordinary pastors cease, yet Christ has not cast off the care of his Church.
send forth labourers into his harvest: Literally, "cast them out": for men are very slow in a work so holy.
